appraisal_events.evidence: « Je n'ai pas vu Mme Berma dans Phèdre, mais j'ai entendu dire qu'elle y était admirable. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois relays secondhand but positive praise of Berma's performance, a hedged endorsement reported rather than personally witnessed.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Aussi n'hésita-t-il pas à m'envoyer chercher un petit poème en prose... Mais elle ne dut pas gagner Norpois, car ce fut sans me dire une parole qu'il me le rendit. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois returns the narrator's cherished prose-poem in complete silence, a pointed non-response that the narrator reads as a dismissal of his literary effort.

appraisal_events.evidence: « En revanche il n'hésita pas à féliciter mon père de la « composition » de son portefeuille « d'un goût très sûr, très délicat, très fin ». »
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois explicitly compliments the father's investment choices, though the narrator's framing (Norpois's satisfaction at seeming to judge others' lesser fortunes generously) casts the praise as partly performative condescension.

status_effects.explanation: Norpois's secondhand but positive report modestly reinforces Berma's reputation, though the assessment is hedged and reported rather than firsthand.
Norpois's silent, wordless return of the narrator's poem quietly diminishes the narrator's standing and confidence as an aspiring writer in this exchange.
Norpois's explicit compliment on the father's portfolio composition, though colored by a note of condescension, publicly affirms the father's taste and competence.

ambiguities: Norpois's praise of the father's portfolio is narrated with an undercutting note about Norpois's own satisfaction in appearing generous toward lesser fortunes, leaving open how much of the compliment is genuine versus performative.
The reference to Berma's performance is secondhand hearsay ('j'ai entendu dire'), making the positive assessment weaker and less certain than a firsthand judgment.
